catalog_quote: A minor syllable is always unstressed and consists of an onset and a neutral vowel (ə) rime which does not bear contrastive tone. [p.18] ... Sui is a tonal language. ... The neutral tone which occurs on unstressed and minor syllables could be counted as an extra lexical tone. [p.21] ... modern Sui itself is not entirely monosyllabic. Our wordlist includes several glosses which elicited iambic sesquisyllabic forms in various locations. [p.24] ... As with sesquisyllables in Sui, Buyang and Burmese, the stress pattern is clearly iambic [pp.24-25] ... Thus we argue that Sui is still essentially a monosyllabic language. [p.25]

new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record (no catalog record and no stress statement held by the project for suii1243). Statement is tied to Central Sui (Sandong, Shuigen village) for the sketch; the sesquisyllabic examples come from eight data points (SD, DJ, PD, AT, TN, SY, JR, TZ) across Sui dialects. Consistent with the compilers note in the mirror same passages, same reading).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Sui is a tone language (6 tones on unchecked syllables, 2 on checked) and largely monosyllabic; the only word-stress statement concerns sesquisyllabic words (reducing compounds / nominal prefixes such as kə0 ʔdjup7 'spirit', qa0- + noun): the minor (reduced) first syllable with schwa is always unstressed and carries a toneless 'neutral tone' (tone 0), the following major syllable is stressed and tone-bearing, i.e. an iambic (final-prominence) pattern within such words. No statement of stress placement for ordinary compounds or polysyllables beyond this.
new_statements.exceptions: Minor syllables 'almost always' precede the major syllable; schwa 'usually occurs without a coda only in a minor syllable and is therefore always short and unstressed' (p.19 / PDF 31); every minor syllable is identifiable with a full major syllable so an underlying tone 'can almost always be ascertained' (p.21 / PDF 33). Appendix G per-data-point phonology sketches (pp.227-254 / PDF 239-266) give initials, finals and tone values only, no stress statement; whole-book a full-text search for stress/accent|unstressed|iambic|accent|prominen|prosod finds linguistic stress statements only on pp.30-37 (other hits are 'accent' = regional accent, 'stress-free' test subjects, 'We stress that').
new_statements.identity_note: Sui [swi], Kam-Sui branch of Tai-Kadai, Sandu county, Guizhou; the phonology sketch is based on Central Sui as spoken in Shuigen village, Sandong township (data point SD, the traditional 'Sandong dialect' standard); the sesquisyllable examples are drawn from eight of the book's sixteen data points across Central, Western, Southern and other Sui dialect areas.

tone_statements.citation: Castro, Andy. 2011. Southern Sui: a fourth Sui dialect. JSEALS 4(2): 1-31.
tone_statements.quote: Sui has six contrastive tones on open syllables and two on closed syllables with different pitch contours depending on the length of the vowel nucleus. Typical tone values for the Sandong dialect are given in Table 1. ... Table 1: Typical Sui tone values (Sandong dialect, Wei & Edmondson 2003:xxviii). Syllable type Tone number Tone value ... open (unchecked) ... 1 11 ... 2 31 ... 3 33 ... 4 51 ... 5 35 ... 6 24 ... closed (checked) (-p, -t, -k codas) 7 35 (long), 55 (short) ... 8 42 (long), 31 (short)
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Eight numbered tones (6 open + 2 checked; Chao values credited to Wei & Edmondson 2003); own field data: Tone 6 = 55 in Southern Sui; fn. 10: a 'neutral' tone (superscript 0) on reduced syllables.

tone_statements.citation: Burusphat, Somsonge, Wei Xuecun (James Wei) & Jerold A. Edmondson (eds.). 2003. Sui (Shui)-Chinese-Thai-English dictionary. Nakhon Pathom: Institute of Language and Culture for Rural Development, Mahidol University. 450 pp. [cited as Wei & Edmondson 2003 by Castro 2011 and as Burusphat, Wei & Edmondson 2003 by Stanford 2011]
tone_statements.quote: Sui tones. Table 1 shows tones of unchecked syllables for speakers in a village in the Sandong Township region. The tone values in Table 1 are based on the author’s research and Zeng & Yao (1996), presented with Chao’s (1930) 1-5 pitch scale. ... [Table 1: Tones in Sandong Township (unchecked syllables): Tone 1 13, Tone 2 31, Tone 3 33, Tone 4 52, Tone 5 35, Tone 6 55] Tone 6 is 24 in some regions, and subtle regional variation in Tone 1 is also reported (discussed below). In all dialects, Tone 6 is high level 55 for recent Chinese loanwords having Mandarin Tone 3. ... Two of the six Sui tones show regional variation: Tone 6 and Tone 1. Tone 6 is highly salient and easy to distinguish as a categorical variable. As Figure 10 shows, Tone 6 is a high-level 55 in some regions and low-rising 24 in other regions. This variable has been stable for 50 years; SDB shows the same regional pattern.

tone_statements.citation: Li, Fang-Kuei. 1948. The distribution of initials and tones in the Sui language. Language 24(2): 160-167. doi:10.2307/409796
tone_statements.quote: Like other Kadai languages, Sui is isolating, largely monosyllabic, and has a system of contour tones. ... The tone reference numbers, e.g., “Tone 1” (T1), “Tone 2” (T2), correspond to the transcription system traditionally applied to Sui ... In that transcription system, Tones T7 and T8 are transcribed for “checked” syllables, referring to syllables ending in /–p, -t, -k/. ... Table 1. Sui Tones from Shuiyu Diaocha Baogao (1956:23). Unchecked Tones ... T1 T2 T3 T4 T5 T6 North 13 31 33 53 35 24* South 13 31 33 53 35 55 *A value of 55 occurs in Chinese loan words.
tone_statements.locator: p. 13 sec. 2.1 and pp. 16-17 sec. 2.1.1 The Sui Tone System, Table 1
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Author counts 'the six Sui tones' (unchecked T1-T6, measured acoustically); checked T7/T8 (S/L) are extra traditional categories, possibly equivalent to unchecked ones. No sandhi reported. At least 70 forms.

tone.quote: Like other Kadai languages, Sui is isolating, largely monosyllabic, and has a system of contour tones. ... The tone reference numbers, e.g., “Tone 1” (T1), “Tone 2” (T2), correspond to the transcription system traditionally applied to Sui ... In that transcription system, Tones T7 and T8 are transcribed for “checked” syllables, referring to syllables ending in /–p, -t, -k/. ... Table 1. Sui Tones from Shuiyu Diaocha Baogao (1956:23). Unchecked Tones ... T1 T2 T3 T4 T5 T6 North 13 31 33 53 35 24* South 13 31 33 53 35 55 *A value of 55 occurs in Chinese loan words.
tone.locator: p. 13 sec. 2.1 and pp. 16-17 sec. 2.1.1 The Sui Tone System, Table 1

tone.quote: Sui has six contrastive tones on open syllables and two on closed syllables with different pitch contours depending on the length of the vowel nucleus. Typical tone values for the Sandong dialect are given in Table 1. ... Table 1: Typical Sui tone values (Sandong dialect, Wei & Edmondson 2003:xxviii). Syllable type Tone number Tone value ... open (unchecked) ... 1 11 ... 2 31 ... 3 33 ... 4 51 ... 5 35 ... 6 24 ... closed (checked) (-p, -t, -k codas) 7 35 (long), 55 (short) ... 8 42 (long), 31 (short)
